findings.quote: A shell is split into **subshells** named $s$, $p$, $d$ and $f$. A subshell is made of **orbitals**, and each orbital holds at most two electrons.
findings.problem: The opening Core Concept paragraph has seven sentences, over the one-to-three-sentence limit. Other paragraphs also run over: the Groups and Periods paragraph on period number (4 sentences), Metals, Nonmetals and Metalloids (5), the shielding and across-a-period paragraphs (4 each), and the atomic radius, first ionization energy, electronegativity and second electron-affinity paragraphs (4 each). Style only; the teaching is complete. Round-2 Blocker on the shielding sentence is fixed: the lesson now says the new electron enters the outer shell only across the main-group elements and the d subshell of the shell below across the transition metals.
